correctness.rationale: With ties retaining the present bit, each actual strict-majority flip reduces the bichromatic-edge count, so no nontrivial recurrence. Fixed states are unanimous colors or (only for both even parts) jointly tied counts; a one-part tie is broken deterministically by the other part's strict majority. For opposite initial strict majorities, exactly a initial one-vertices on the first shore and c=n-b initial zero-vertices on second shore are eligible; their first individual update times form a uniformly ordered permutation. First shore loses strict positive majority after r=a-floor(m/2) flips, second gains positive majority after s=ceil(n/2)-b flips. The second shore reaching s first corresponds to a winning prefix with j<r first-shore flips and yields the displayed finite sum of falling factorial weights. Exact color-complement handles reverse orientation. Order statistics show odd-odd polarization symmetry and even-sided tie advantages; fixed-n limit follows from binomial tails. Independently solved rational Markov count-state equations for 729 initial macrostate cases for m,n<=6; tests include even-even ties. Finite checks do not prove all m,n.
